questions.question: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, proclaimed in August 1789, stated, 'Men are born and remain free and equal in rights. Social distinctions may be founded only upon the general good.' This declaration most directly challenged which fundamental aspect of the Ancien Régime?

options.text: The absolute authority of the King.
options.explanation: The declaration challenged the absolute monarchy but not as directly as the legal inequalities of the Estates.

options.text: The system of hereditary privileges and the legal inequality of the Estates.
options.explanation: Correct. The declaration directly challenged the legal inequalities of the Ancien Régime.

options.text: The economic dominance of the bourgeoisie.
options.explanation: The declaration did not directly address the economic dominance of the bourgeoisie.

options.text: The influence of the Catholic Church in state affairs.
options.explanation: The declaration challenged the Church's privileges indirectly but not as its primary focus.

questions.explanation: While the Declaration also implicitly challenged the absolute monarchy and promoted other freedoms, the phrase 'Social distinctions may be founded only upon the general good' directly attacked the core principle of the Ancien Régime: the existence of legally recognized hereditary privileges and distinctions for the First and Second Estates (clergy and nobility) that were not based on merit or the common welfare, but on birth. This was a cornerstone of the legal inequality that the Revolution sought to dismantle.
questions.hint: The declaration opposed hereditary privileges and legal inequalities.
